easy.def: A thick, flat piece of something.
examples: A slab of stone.
A slab of cake.
He lifted the slab.

more.def: A thick, flat piece of something, such as stone, wood or food.
examples: A slab of stone served as a bench in the park.
He cut a thick slab of cheese for his sandwich.
A concrete slab was laid for the new garage.

easy.def: Loose, not tight.
examples: The rope is slack.
The sail was slack.
The line went slack.

more.def: Not pulled tight, or loose.
examples: The rope hung slack between the posts.
The sail was slack with no wind.
The fishing line went slack.

easy.def: To become looser or slower.
examples: The rope slackened.
The wind slackened.
He slackened his pace.

more.def: To become looser, slower or less strong.
examples: The rope slackened when I let go.
The wind slackened and the sails drooped.
He slackened his pace as he got tired.

easy.def: To shut with a loud bang.
examples: The door slammed.
He slammed the door.
The wind slams the gate.

more.def: To shut or hit something hard so that it makes a loud noise.
examples: The wind slammed the door shut.
Please do not slam the car door.
He slammed the book on the desk.

easy.def: Casual words that friends use when they talk.
examples: "Cool" is slang for good.
Slang changes over time.
I learned some new slang.

more.def: Informal words and phrases that people use in everyday talk, but not in formal writing.
examples: Words like "awesome" are examples of slang.
Slang changes quickly, so older people may not know new words.
The author used slang to make her characters sound real.

easy.def: To lean to one side.
examples: The roof will slant.
Her writing slants.
The floor slanted.

more.def: To lean or slope in one direction instead of going straight up.
examples: The old roof slants down to the garden.
Her handwriting slants to the right.
The sun slanted through the window in the afternoon.

easy.def: A slope, or a leaning line.
examples: The roof has a slant.
There is a slant to the hill.
The slant of the floor was steep.

more.def: A sloping direction, or the way something leans.
examples: The slant of the roof lets the snow slide off.
The floor had a slight slant.
She wrote with a slant to the right.

easy.def: To hit something with a flat hand.
examples: I slap the water.
He slapped a mosquito.
The wave slapped the boat.

more.def: To hit something with the flat of your hand, with a sharp sound.
examples: She slapped the water to make a splash.
He slapped the mosquito on his arm.
The waves slapped against the side of the boat.

easy.def: To cut with a long, quick swing.
examples: The farmer will slash the weeds.
She slashed the tape with scissors.
He slashed the air with a stick.

more.def: To cut with a long, quick sweep; also to lower something by a large amount.
examples: The gardener slashed through the tall weeds with a machete.
The store slashed prices to sell the old coats.
The explorer slashed a path through the thick jungle.

easy.def: A leaning line, like this: /
examples: A slash is on the keyboard.
Put a slash between the words.
Type a slash here.

more.def: A slanting mark (/) used in writing to show a choice or to divide parts of a web address.
examples: Use a slash between and/or to show a choice.
The web address has a slash after the dot-com.
The date was written with slashes, like 4/5/2025.

easy.def: A thin, flat piece of wood or metal.
examples: The fence has slats.
The slats are wood.
A slat broke.

more.def: A thin, flat strip of wood, metal or plastic.
examples: The blind is made of thin slats.
A slat in the fence was loose.
The bed has wooden slats under the mattress.

easy.def: A smooth gray stone that splits into thin sheets.
examples: The roof is made of slate.
The slate is gray.
A slate fell.

more.def: A smooth, dark gray rock that splits easily into flat layers and is used for roofs and old blackboards.
examples: The old school had a roof of slate.
Children in the past wrote on slate boards with chalk.
The path was paved with flat pieces of slate.

easy.def: A person who is owned by another and must work for free.
examples: Long ago, many slaves worked on farms.
Slavery was cruel and unfair.
The book tells about a slave who ran to freedom.

more.def: A person who was treated as property and forced to work without freedom or pay.
examples: Harriet Tubman helped many slaves escape to freedom.
In the past, slaves were bought and sold, which was wrong and cruel.
Our class read a story about a slave who learned to read in secret.

easy.def: A time when people were owned by others and forced to work.
examples: We learned about slavery.
Slavery was wrong.
Slavery ended long ago.

more.def: A system in which people are owned by others and forced to work without pay; it is cruel and wrong.
examples: We learned in history class that slavery was wrong.
Many brave people worked to end slavery.
Slavery ended in the United States after the Civil War.

easy.def: A small vehicle that slides over snow.
examples: I love my new sled.
The sled is red.
We pulled the sled.

more.def: A flat or low vehicle with long, smooth runners for sliding over snow or ice.
examples: I rode a sled down the hill.
We pulled the sled up the snowy slope.
The dogs pulled a sled across the ice.

easy.def: To ride down a snowy hill.
examples: We sled down the hill.
They sledded all day.
I like to sled.

more.def: To ride down a snowy hill on a low vehicle with runners.
examples: We sled down the big hill after the snow.
They sledded all afternoon until it got dark.
I like to sled with my cousins in winter.

easy.def: A sled.
examples: We rode a sledge.
The sledge slid.
A sledge is a sled.

more.def: A vehicle on runners for traveling on snow, or a large hammer.
examples: We pulled the sledge up the hill.
The dogs pulled the sledge across the snow.
A sledge carried the wood.

easy.def: A big, heavy hammer.
examples: The man used a sledgehammer.
A sledgehammer is heavy.
The worker swung a sledgehammer.

more.def: A large, heavy hammer used with both hands to break rocks or drive posts.
examples: Workers used a sledgehammer to break the old wall.
He needed both hands to lift the sledgehammer.
The sledgehammer drove the post into the ground.

easy.def: Smooth and shiny.
examples: The cat has sleek fur.
A sleek car drove by.
The seal is sleek.

more.def: Smooth, shiny and neat in shape.
examples: The cat's sleek fur shone in the sun.
A sleek sports car sped down the road.
The seal was sleek and quick in the water.

easy.def: To rest with your eyes closed.
examples: I sleep at night.
The baby is sleeping.
The cat slept all day.

more.def: To rest your body and mind with your eyes closed, as you do at night.
examples: Bears sleep through most of the winter.
I slept well after the long hike.
Please be quiet because the baby is sleeping.

easy.def: The rest you get at night.
examples: I need sleep.
She got a good sleep.
He fell into a deep sleep.

more.def: The natural rest that your body needs every night.
examples: Children need a lot of sleep to grow and learn.
I fell into a deep sleep as soon as my head touched the pillow.
A good night of sleep helps you feel ready for school.

easy.def: A person who is asleep.
examples: The sleeper did not wake.
A sound sleeper.
The sleeper snored.

more.def: A person who is sleeping, or a train car with beds in it.
examples: She is a sound sleeper who never wakes up in the night.
The train had a sleeper car with small beds for the trip.
The noise did not wake the sleeper.

easy.def: In a way that shows you are tired.
examples: He yawned sleepily.
She rubbed her eyes sleepily.
The baby smiled sleepily.

more.def: In a drowsy way, as if you are about to fall asleep.
examples: She yawned sleepily and snuggled into her pillow.
The little boy walked sleepily to the table.
The cat blinked sleepily in the warm sun.

easy.def: Not able to sleep.
examples: I had a sleepless night.
The sleepless baby cried.
He was sleepless.

more.def: Without sleep, or unable to sleep.
examples: The storm gave us a sleepless night.
The excited boy was sleepless before the trip.
She had a sleepless night worrying about the test.

easy.def: When a friend sleeps at your house.
examples: I had a sleepover.
We have a sleepover Friday.
The sleepover was fun.

more.def: A party where friends spend the night at one person's home.
examples: I had a sleepover for my birthday and six friends came.
We watched a movie and ate popcorn at the sleepover.
The sleepover lasted until the next morning.

easy.def: To walk while you are asleep.
examples: Some people sleepwalk.
She sleepwalked.
He might sleepwalk.

more.def: To get up and walk around while you are still asleep.
examples: My cousin used to sleepwalk when he was little.
She sleepwalked to the kitchen and back to bed.
Some people sleepwalk when they are very tired.

easy.def: Needing to sleep.
examples: I am sleepy.
The sleepy baby yawned.
She felt sleepy.

more.def: Feeling tired and ready to go to sleep.
examples: The baby was sleepy after her bath.
I felt sleepy after the long car ride.
The sleepy puppy curled up in its bed.

easy.def: A sleepy person.
examples: Wake up, sleepyhead!
Our sleepyhead naps.
The sleepyhead yawned.

more.def: A friendly name for someone who is sleepy.
examples: Wake up, sleepyhead, it is time for school.
The baby is a little sleepyhead.
The sleepyhead yawned and stretched.

easy.def: Rain that freezes into little pieces of ice.
examples: The sleet fell.
Sleet is cold.
We walked in the sleet.

more.def: Rain that is partly frozen as it falls, in small pieces of ice.
examples: The sleet made the road slippery.
We walked home in the cold sleet.
Sleet tapped against the window.

easy.def: The part of a shirt that covers your arm.
examples: The sleeve is long.
I rolled up my sleeve.
My sleeve is torn.

more.def: The part of a piece of clothing that covers your arm.
examples: I rolled up my sleeves to wash dishes.
The sleeve of his coat was torn.
She wiped her nose on her sleeve.

easy.def: A large sled pulled by horses or reindeer.
examples: The sleigh is fast.
A sleigh has bells.
We rode in a sleigh.

more.def: A large vehicle on runners that is pulled by horses or other animals over snow.
examples: The sleigh slid over the snow.
A sleigh with bells on it jingled down the road.
In the song, a sleigh pulled by reindeer flies through the sky.

easy.def: Thin in a nice way.
examples: The tree is slender.
She has slender fingers.
A slender vase.

more.def: Thin and graceful.
examples: She has long, slender fingers.
A slender vase held one flower.
The slender tree swayed in the breeze.

easy.def: A person who finds clues, a detective.
examples: The sleuth found a clue.
A sleuth looks for clues.
The sleuth solved it.

more.def: A detective, or a person who looks for clues.
examples: The sleuth found the missing key.
A young sleuth solved the mystery in the book.
The sleuth looked at the muddy footprints.

easy.def: A lot of something.
examples: I have a slew of homework.
A slew of cards arrived.
We saw a slew of birds.

more.def: A large number of things.
examples: She got a slew of cards on her birthday.
A slew of ducks landed on the pond.
He had a slew of questions about the trip.

easy.def: A thin, flat piece cut from something.
examples: I ate a slice of pizza.
The slice of bread is thin.
I want a slice of cake.

more.def: A thin, flat piece that has been cut from something larger.
examples: She cut a thin slice of ham for the sandwich.
Dad put a slice of cheese on the bread.
She cut a slice of watermelon.

easy.def: To cut into thin pieces.
examples: I slice the apple.
She sliced the bread.
Please slice the tomato.

more.def: To cut something into thin, flat pieces.
examples: Mom sliced the bread for sandwiches.
He sliced the apple into eight pieces.
The chef sliced the tomatoes.

easy.def: Smooth and wet.
examples: The road is slick.
The ice is slick.
The floor was slick.

more.def: Smooth and wet so that it is slippery.
examples: The road was slick with rain.
The floor was slick, so I walked carefully.
Slick ice covered the steps.

easy.def: A raincoat.
examples: He wore a yellow slicker.
The slicker is shiny.
She put on her slicker.

more.def: A long raincoat made of shiny material that keeps out the rain.
examples: He wore a yellow slicker in the rain.
The sailor's slicker kept him dry on the boat.
She hung her wet slicker by the door.

easy.def: To move smoothly over a surface.
examples: I slide on the ice.
The sled slides down the hill.
He slid on the floor.

more.def: To move smoothly and quietly along a surface.
examples: The kids slid down the snowy hill on sleds.
The drawer slides open easily.
He slid across the floor in his socks.

easy.def: A smooth, slanted toy that you go down.
examples: I go down the slide.
The slide is fun.
We played on the slide.

more.def: A smooth, slanted play structure that children climb up and come down on.
examples: The children took turns on the slide at the park.
The slide is so tall that you can see the whole playground.
The little girl climbed the ladder and zoomed down the slide.

easy.def: Something that slides.
examples: The slider moves.
Drag the slider to change the sound.
He used the slider on the screen.

more.def: A thing that slides, such as a part of a control, or a small round sandwich.
examples: Move the slider to turn up the music.
The pitcher threw a slider that dipped low.
We ate sliders at the picnic.

easy.def: Small.
examples: There was a slight breeze.
A slight change is fine.
I felt a slight pain.

more.def: Small in size or amount.
examples: A slight breeze moved the curtains.
There is a slight chance of rain.
She felt a slight pain in her toe.

easy.def: A little.
examples: I am slightly tired.
The door was slightly open.
It is slightly cold.

more.def: To a small degree.
examples: He was slightly late for school.
I felt slightly sick after eating too fast.
The soup was slightly too salty.

easy.def: Thin in a nice way.
examples: The slim tree sways.
She has a slim book.
The slim bike is fast.

more.def: Thin and narrow.
examples: The slim tree swayed in the wind.
She tucked a slim book into her bag.
The path between the two walls was slim.

easy.def: A thick, wet, slippery goo.
examples: The snail left slime.
I made green slime.
The frog was covered in slime.

more.def: A thick, wet and slippery substance, such as the goo on a snail or a fish, or a toy made to be gooey.
examples: A snail left a trail of slime across the garden path.
The rocks in the pond were covered with green slime.
We mixed glue and water to make a bowl of slime.

easy.def: Wet, slippery and gooey.
examples: The snail is slimy.
I touched a slimy rock.
The frog felt slimy.

more.def: Covered with a wet, slippery, sticky layer, like the coating on a snail or a fish.
examples: The rocks at the bottom of the creek were green and slimy.
A snail left a slimy trail across the garden path.
The frog's slimy skin slipped right through my fingers.

easy.def: A strip of cloth that holds an arm up.
examples: He wore a sling on his arm.
The sling held her arm.
The sling is blue.

more.def: A band of cloth that hangs from the neck to support a hurt arm, or a strap for carrying something.
examples: He wore a sling on his arm for two weeks.
She carried the baby in a sling.
A rope sling lifted the box.

easy.def: To throw something with a swinging movement.
examples: I sling my bag over my shoulder.
He slung the rope.
She slung the towel.

more.def: To throw something carelessly, or to hang it with a swing.
examples: I slung my backpack over my shoulder.
He slung the rope over the branch.
She slung her towel around her neck.

easy.def: To move quietly so no one notices.
examples: The cat will slink away.
The dog slunk off.
He slunk out of the room.

more.def: To move quietly and slowly, as if trying not to be seen.
examples: The cat slunk under the porch.
The fox slunk through the tall grass.
He slunk out of the room when he saw the mess.

easy.def: To slide by accident.
examples: Do not slip on the ice.
He slipped on the wet floor.
The soap slipped from my hand.

more.def: To slide by accident and almost fall, or to slide out of place.
examples: Be careful not to slip on the icy steps.
The cup slipped out of my wet hands.
She slipped on a banana peel in the cartoon.

easy.def: To move quietly.
examples: She slipped out the door.
The cat slipped into the room.
He slipped away.

more.def: To move quietly or without being noticed.
examples: The cat slipped through the open door.
She slipped a note into his bag.
We slipped out of the room as the baby slept.

easy.def: A soft shoe you wear indoors.
examples: I wear slippers at home.
The slipper is warm.
My slippers are fuzzy.

more.def: A soft, light shoe that is worn indoors.
examples: I wear my slippers around the house.
Her slippers were warm and fuzzy.
The dog chewed my slipper.

easy.def: So wet or smooth that you might slide.
examples: The ice is slippery.
The wet floor is slippery.
A fish is slippery to hold.

more.def: So smooth, wet, or icy that it is hard to hold or walk on.
examples: Be careful, because the floor is slippery when it is wet.
The soap was too slippery to hold.
Wet leaves made the sidewalk slippery.

easy.def: A long, narrow cut or opening.
examples: There is a slit in the bag.
The mail goes in a slit.
A slit in the tent lets in air.

more.def: A long, thin cut or opening.
examples: The mail slipped through the slit in the door.
A small slit in the tent let in a cool breeze.
The cat peered through a slit in the fence.

easy.def: To make a long, thin cut.
examples: Slit the bag open.
She slit the tape.
Dad slits the box.

more.def: To cut something open with a long, thin cut.
examples: He slit the envelope open with a letter opener.
She slit the tape on the box to open it.
The baker slit the top of the loaf before baking.

easy.def: To move by sliding along the ground, like a snake.
examples: The snake will slither.

Worms slither.

more.def: To glide along a surface in a twisting way, like a snake.
examples: The snake slithered through the grass.
An eel slithered across the muddy bank.
A worm slithered over the damp soil.

easy.def: A thin little piece.
examples: I got a sliver in my finger.
A sliver of wood.
Mom cut a sliver of pie.

more.def: A thin, small, sharp piece that has broken off something.
examples: I got a sliver of wood in my finger.
Mom cut me a sliver of cake.

easy.def: To let spit run out of your mouth.
examples: The dog will slobber.

My puppy slobbers on me.

more.def: To let saliva drip from the mouth.
examples: The big dog slobbered all over my hand.
The baby slobbered on her bib.
My puppy slobbers when it sees food.

easy.def: Spit that runs from the mouth.
examples: The dog left slobber on my hand.
The baby had slobber on her chin.
There was slobber on the toy.

more.def: Saliva that drips from the mouth, especially of a baby or dog.
examples: The dog left slobber on my sleeve.
A bib caught the baby's slobber.
I wiped the slobber off the ball.

easy.def: To walk with great effort.
examples: We slogged through the mud.

more.def: To walk or work with great effort through something hard.
examples: We slogged through the deep mud.
The hikers slogged up the steep hill.
He slogged through the long homework.

easy.def: A short saying that is easy to remember.
examples: Our team has a slogan.
The slogan is on the poster.

more.def: A short, catchy phrase that a group or company uses to be remembered or to tell people what it believes.
examples: Our school's slogan is on a banner above the front doors.

easy.def: To spill over the edge.

Do not slop the milk.

more.def: To spill liquid over the edge of something, or to splash it around.
examples: The soup slopped over the side of the bowl.

Don't slop the paint on the floor.

easy.def: A surface that goes up or down at a slant.
examples: We slid down the slope.
The slope is steep.
Snow covered the slope.

more.def: A surface that is higher at one end than the other.
examples: We slid down the snowy slope on a sled.
The roof has a steep slope so that rain runs off.
Skiers raced down the slope.

easy.def: To go up or down at a slant.
examples: The roof slopes down.
The hill slopes.
The land slopes to the lake.

more.def: To rise or fall at an angle.
examples: The roof slopes down toward the porch.

easy.def: Messy and careless.

more.def: Done in a careless way, or messy and wet.
examples: His handwriting was sloppy and hard to read.
The sloppy painter got paint on the floor.
The sandwich was so sloppy it dripped.

easy.def: To splash around.
examples: The water sloshed.
I slosh through puddles.
Milk sloshed in the pail.

more.def: To move around in a splashing way, as liquid does.
examples: Water sloshed in the bucket as I walked.
I sloshed through the puddles in my boots.
The milk sloshed over the side.

easy.def: A narrow opening.
examples: Put a coin in the slot.
The slot is thin.
Drop the letter in the slot.

more.def: A narrow opening or space that something fits into.
examples: Slide your ticket into the slot at the gate.
The mail drops through a slot in the door.
The card fits into the slot.

easy.def: A slow animal that hangs from trees.

The sloth hangs in a tree.
We saw a sloth.

more.def: A slow-moving animal of South and Central America that hangs upside down from tree branches and eats leaves.
examples: The sloth hung upside down from the branch, moving very slowly.
A sloth sleeps most of the day.

easy.def: To sit or stand with your back bent.

more.def: To sit, stand or walk with your shoulders and back drooping.

easy.def: Not fast.

more.def: Moving or happening at a low speed, or taking a long time.

easy.def: To go less fast.
examples: Slow down, please.

Cars slow near the school.

more.def: To lower the speed of something, or to move at a lower speed.

easy.def: Not fast.
examples: The turtle walks slowly.

Please speak slowly.

more.def: At a slow speed, taking a long time.

easy.def: Thick, soft mud or dirt.

more.def: Thick, soft, wet mud or dirty waste.

easy.def: A slimy animal with no shell.

more.def: A soft, slimy, crawling animal like a snail but with no shell.

easy.def: A baseball player who hits the ball very hard.

He is a slugger.

more.def: A baseball player who hits the ball very hard and far.
examples: The slugger hit the ball over the fence.

easy.def: Slow and not lively.
examples: I feel sluggish.

more.def: Slow-moving and lacking energy.
examples: I felt sluggish after a big lunch.

easy.def: Sleep.

more.def: A peaceful sleep, often a deep one.

easy.def: To sleep.
examples: The cat slumbers in the sun.

more.def: To sleep, especially peacefully.

easy.def: To sit or fall down heavily.

more.def: To sink or fall down heavily, often because you are tired or sad.

easy.def: Half-melted snow.

easy.def: Half melted, like wet snow.
examples: The road was slushy.
Slushy snow.
The slushy path.

more.def: Partly melted and wet, like snow on a warm day.
examples: The slushy road splashed our boots.
We walked through slushy snow on the way home.
The slushy path was hard to cross.

easy.def: Clever in a quiet, tricky way.
examples: The sly fox hid.
She gave a sly smile.
A sly cat watched the bird.

more.def: Clever in a quiet, secret way that makes you good at tricking others.
examples: The sly fox crept up on the henhouse while the farmer slept.
She gave a sly grin when she hid her brother's shoe.
The sly cat waited in the grass for the bird to land.

easy.def: In a sneaky, clever way.
examples: The fox smiled slyly.
She slyly winked.
He slyly took a cookie.

more.def: In a clever, secret way, often with a smile.
examples: The fox grinned slyly at the hens.
She slyly slipped a note into his bag.
He slyly winked at his sister.
